response: Causal chain: (1) instruction present -> (2) at completion time the agent re-reads the full task and docstrings -> (3) clauses that decayed from working context are re-encoded while a complete implementation exists -> (4) the agent detects mismatches and fixes them within remaining budget -> (5) held-out pass rate rises. The load-bearing assumption is that omissions are forgotten-after-read rather than never-encoded: a re-read of text the model already failed to parse correctly may fail identically (same-reader-same-error). Second fragile link is 4: late fixes need remaining turns; the instruction should shift failures from 'requirement absent' to 'requirement partially handled', which is observable in grader detail. Supporting evidence: positive paired delta; transcripts showing a real re-read (quoting or paraphrasing clauses) followed by concrete fixes; grader failures on candidate arms skewing toward partially-implemented rather than absent behaviors. Disconfirming: identical failure sets across arms with the re-read present in transcripts, which would establish never-encoded as the dominant omission mechanism and cap this whole intervention family.
